transcript: Yesterday, Paul and I saw Cult of Love on Broadway. This is a new play by Leslye Headland about the Dahl family gathering for Christmas in Connecticut. If you like family dramas that bring gasps and laughs, this will be up your alley. It’s a familiar concept: A dysfunctional family with some plus ones try to get through the holidays, but remain hopelessly and hilariously triggered by one another. The siblings are all grown up, they've got their own lives and their own problems, and they are irrevocably different. But, against all odds, love and good old family trauma keeps them tied together. This play doesn't reinvent the wheel, but what it may lack in novelty it certainly has in potency and performances. The writing, though not as heightened as a family drama like Appropriate, is well-grounded for this group of people. It flows nicely, it's well paced, and the ensemble work is seamless. There's no dead air and everyone's living through the conversations, the confrontations, and the tense silences. Chalk that up to the direction and a pretty stacked cast. The use of music in the household is a smart and efficient way to illustrate the bonds and experiences shared by the family members, not to mention that it's fitting for a Christmas gathering and given the family's religious background. Religion is one of the main catalysts for conflict in the play, if it wasn't already implied by the title. I'm sure plenty of folks and audience know these kinds of conflicts all too well, so you've been warned. But, I promise it's also funny. Cult of Love is running at The Hayes into next February. With that, another playbill for my collection.
